AI Maps Global Methane Emissions from Space with NASA's EMIT Instrument

2026-09-09 Vishal Batchu (Google Research) methane emissions, MAPL-EMIT, deep learning, NASA EMIT, PNAS, climate, Earth Engine, greenhouse gas
Read the source article

Quick summary

Google and NASA JPL introduced MAPL-EMIT, an AI model that detects 50% more methane plumes than human experts by analyzing satellite imagery, identifying over 23,000 additional plumes globally.

Key takeaways

  • MAPL-EMIT is a deep learning model from Google Research and NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, published in PNAS
  • Trained on 3.6 million physics-simulated methane plumes, it detects 50% more plumes than human experts
  • The model identified over 23,000 additional plumes globally, including 24 of the 25 world's largest-emitting landfills
  • Methane has 30 times the warming potential of CO2 over a 100-year timeframe
  • Google released the global plume database on Earth Engine, with open-source models on Kaggle and GitHub
